final.title: The Stilling of the Dark Water
final.logline: Tara presses her open hand down, and a dark swell below her flattens into glassy water carrying one bright line of stars.
final.hook: The calm starry portrait holds for a heartbeat, then one heavy dark swell heaves up along the bottom edge as her open hand lowers toward it with a stern, level gaze.
final.story: Tara's name is read as the star that guides, the saviour, and the one who ferries across the ocean of worldly existence. This clip is a symbolic picture of that crossing, not a fixed traditional scene. Rough dark water rises below her, her hand presses down toward it, and it goes glassy with one bright line of stars laid across it like a path. Her gaze is direct and stern, so she reads as a rescuer and not a gentle ornament. A devotional tradition, not found in the main Puranic accounts and told in different versions, says she saved Shiva from the poison of the churned ocean. The clip only echoes that tale. Blue skin, third eye, tiger-skin wrap, skull garland and serpent ornaments stay clear. Her loose hair is a stylisation; traditional images show matted locks or a single braid.
final.loop: The last frame is a held image of still black water holding a line of stars beneath her, mirroring the starry sky of the first frame. The restart to the bare portrait reads as the water becoming sky again, so the rough water can rise anew.
final.share_trigger: Devotees of Tara and people curious about the ten great wisdom goddesses send it as a clear image of her as rescuer and ferrier across. Viewers who love satisfying moments of rough water going still share it too.
final.caption_hook: Tara, second of the ten great wisdom goddesses, is the star that guides and the one who ferries across. Her loose hair here is a stylisation; traditional images show matted locks or a single braid.
final.audio: A deep, heavy water rumble that drops to a hush the moment her hand stops. A soft low drone follows, with one clear, gentle tone as the line of stars appears.

concept.title: She Stills the Dark Sea
concept.logline: Tara raises one steady hand and the dark, churning sea behind her goes still, mirroring the stars.
concept.hook: In the first second a dark sea rises into view behind her, its swells rolling restlessly, as her stern gaze holds and her hand begins to lift against the danger.
concept.story: Tara's name is read as star, as saviour, and as the one who ferries you across the ocean of worldly life. She is the second of the ten great wisdom goddesses, a protector who steps in when danger comes suddenly. A rough dark sea is the danger. Her raised open palm is a guarding gesture, and the sea stills into a mirror of her stars, so the crossing becomes visible as a calm, star-lit water. Her three eyes stay stern and watchful, and her blue skin, tiger-skin wrap, skull garland and serpent ornaments stay in view, so she reads as a fierce guardian. This is a symbolic scene, not a fixed temple image. Her hair is shown loose, while tradition more often shows it matted or in a single braid. One devotional telling also says she calmed the poison of the churning sea, and versions of that tale differ.
concept.loop: The final frame is her centered portrait with the same star-filled sky, now doubled in the still water, so the ending looks like the opening sky made whole. When the clip restarts, the sky returns to its first stillness and the dark sea rises again, so the calm at the end feeds straight back into the threat at the start.
concept.share_trigger: Sent to someone in a frightening or stormy stretch, such as a hard diagnosis, a night journey or a crisis at home, with a line like 'may she still this for you.' It is a protector image, saved and sent by people who know her as the one who guards you from sudden danger.
concept.caption_hook: Tara, second of the ten great wisdom goddesses, is the star, the saviour and the one who ferries you across. Here her raised hand stills a dark sea. A symbolic scene, with her hair loose where tradition shows it matted or braided.
concept.audio: A low, deep rumble of restless water and a held, tense drone at the start. As her hand reaches full height, the rumble drops away to a hush, and one deep, clear bell tone sounds and rings out over a soft, steady hum until the end.

shots.camera: Straight-on at eye level, locked off, waist-up, crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: A dark sea rises into view behind her, its horizon at chest height and its swells rolling restlessly on both sides of her body. Her three eyes hold the viewer in a stern, steady gaze as her right hand lifts slowly to chest height with the palm open and facing forward, and as it rises the swells begin to slow and flatten.
shots.purpose: The problem is on screen from the first second: a dark rough sea. One large, slow gesture is the cause, and the calming water is the visible effect, easy to read on a small screen.

shots.camera: Same straight-on eye-level framing, locked off, crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: Her hand holds steady at chest height, palm forward, and the sea goes fully still, so the stars of the night sky appear in the water and a bright band of reflected starlight spreads across the calm surface on both sides of her. Her stern gaze stays on the viewer as the clip ends on this held image.
shots.purpose: The payoff is a before and after: restless dark water becomes a still, star-filled mirror. It shows protection from danger and a safe crossing in one clear change, and the final frame echoes the opening sky.

concept.title: The Path Across
concept.logline: Tara slowly extends her open hand toward us, and a narrow path of starlight spreads across the dark water to our feet.
concept.hook: In the first second her open hand rises from below the frame toward the viewer, and a faint shimmer of black water slides into the lower edge of the frame.
concept.story: Tara is the one who ferries across the ocean of hardship. She doesn't pull anyone out of the dark; she shows the way over it. The starlight path is that promise, drawn straight toward the person watching.
concept.loop: The path of light softens, her hand returns to rest below the frame, and the water sinks out of view. She is left alone in the starry sky as in the opening frame, ready for the gesture to begin again.
concept.share_trigger: Sent to a friend in a hard season, with the message 'there is a way across, keep going.' It also suits people who feel lost at night or are facing a big change.
concept.caption_hook: When the night feels too wide to cross, look for the star that shows you the way.
concept.audio: A low, steady drone with soft water lapping. A single clear bell-like chime sounds as the path of light reaches the viewer.

shots.camera: Straight-on at eye level, locked off, waist-up, crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: Her steady gaze meets the viewer. Her open hand slowly rises from below the frame and extends toward the viewer, and as it opens, a glossy surface of calm black water slides into the lower edge of the frame. Her black hair settles gradually under its own weight.
shots.purpose: Starts visible motion within 1.5 seconds. The gesture asks for trust, and the water introduces the ocean she must be seen to cross.

shots.camera: Same straight-on eye-level framing, locked off, crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: Her hand holds open and steady toward the viewer, and a narrow path of starlight spreads across the black water, running from beneath her hand to the bottom of the frame. Soft ripples move outward from the path. Then her hand lowers slowly, the path fades gently, and the frame returns to her portrait.
shots.purpose: The payoff is one clear image: a path of light made by her hand. The slow fade and lowered hand return to the opening frame so the clip loops.

feedback: virality: Hook is a slow rise of a hand from below frame. It is motion, but it is a 'hand rises' gesture, not a surprising event. The black water 'slides' into the bottom edge as a faint shimmer, which is barely visible on a phone.

virality: The payoff (starlight path) does not begin until shot 2, about second 4. The first 4 seconds are a hand rising and a calm surface appearing. That is a long wait for a viewer who has not yet seen what the hand does.

virality: Geometry is confused. The path runs 'from beneath her hand to the bottom of the frame' in a locked waist-up portrait where her hand points at the camera. A path toward the lens in a straight-on shot foreshortens to a thin strip at the bottom edge. The 'path to our feet' idea may not read at all, and the model may render it as a vague glow.
virality: Loop is soft. The hand lowers, the path fades and the water sinks, so the end is an ebb and the beginning is a rise. A viewer can't tell the clip has restarted, which gives no rewatch pull.

virality: Closest to the dossier's recommended beat, and the path of starlight is a recognisable image, but 'open hand extended' is still the generic goddess-blessing gesture the rubric warns against. The consequence arrives late.
virality: Send-worthiness is good: 'there is a way across' is a clear message for a friend in a hard season. Save value is moderate, since it is a pleasant image rather than something to keep.

authenticity: Core idea (ferrying across the ocean of existence, star as guide) matches the dossier's etymology and purpose, and it is non-graphic and reverent. But the dossier says the 'ferries across' reading is one of three etymologies that vary by source, and the story states it as flat fact ('Tara is the one who ferries across...').

authenticity: The story line 'She doesn't pull anyone out of the dark; she shows the way over it' is invented theology. Tara is also the saviour who rescues (the poison story, Ugra Tara protecting from sudden danger), so this contrast narrows her and partly contradicts the dossier's 'rescue' emphasis.

authenticity: The dossier says the locked anchor has loose flowing hair, which departs from the matted jata or single braid. The repeated 'black hair settles under its own weight' perpetuates that mismatch. The shots never mention her iconic features (blue skin, third eye, tiger skin, skull garland), so a viewer could take her for a generic goddess.

authenticity: The share trigger and caption lean toward secular self-help ('keep going', 'the night feels too wide') and say nothing of devotion. This is mild, but it drifts from her tantric identity, and Tara is also associated with cremation grounds and wrathful protection, which are entirely absent.
authenticity: The open outstretched hand is a pan-Indic blessing/giving gesture. The dossier lists no hand-object set or fixed mudra for her, so it should not be presented as her signature gesture.

feasibility: Too many moving elements: rising hand, water sliding in, spreading starlight path, outward ripples, then a hand lowering and the path fading. That is at least four on top of the hair, against a limit of two.
feasibility: The hand extends toward the camera from below frame. Foreshortened hands moving toward the lens are a known weak spot, and the hand will likely distort or morph as it opens.

feasibility: Geometry does not work. In a locked-off, eye-level, waist-up shot, a water surface 'slides in' at the bottom edge and a path of light runs 'from beneath her hand to the bottom of the frame'. There is no coherent ground plane, and the water has no source or cause.

feasibility: The water and the starlight path are entirely new content that is not in the reference portrait. They have to be invented mid-clip, and the path's appearance is only loosely tied to the hand's gesture.
feasibility: Returning the hand below the frame, sinking the water out of view and landing back on the exact opening frame is a fragile reverse sequence.
feasibility: The two-shot split (4 s and 6 s) and the 'within 1.5 seconds' hook rely on timing, and the shot split reads like a cut. It should be one continuous clip.

virality fix: Make the path of light the hook. Open on the hand already extended, with the first star-stepping stones igniting one by one across the black water within 1 second, so the consequence is visible immediately.

virality fix: Change the camera or composition so the path reads on a phone screen. Use a slight high angle or have the path run vertically up the frame toward her palm, so the lit line is large and unmistakable.
virality fix: Shorten the setup. Drop the separate 'hand rises' beat. Spend about 3 seconds on the path forming and 5 on the lit path holding and pulsing.
virality fix: Build a real loop. End on the path dissolving back into starry water and her palm reaching the same raised position as the first frame, so the last frame cuts cleanly into the first.
virality fix: Cut the instruction that the hair 'settles under its own weight'. It adds a render risk and no payoff.
authenticity fix: Soften the etymology claim to 'one of the meanings of her name is the one who ferries across', or word it as 'devotees know her as...'.
authenticity fix: Drop the 'doesn't pull anyone out' line. Use 'she guides and carries across' so the rescue aspect is preserved.
authenticity fix: Keep the blue skin, third eye and tiger-skin wrap visible in the opening frame. Either fix the hair to jata/Ekajata or avoid drawing attention to the hair motion.
authenticity fix: Add one line in the caption or story tying the image to Tara by name, as star, saviour and ferrier, so the clip reads as devotional and not generic.
authenticity fix: Do not call the open hand her signature mudra. Present it as an invitation.

feasibility fix: Cut it to two moving elements: the hand opening slowly and a starlight path appearing. Drop the ripples and the sliding water, or have the water already be a faint dark band at the bottom of the reference portrait.
feasibility fix: Keep the hand at chest height with the palm open sideways or upward, rather than reaching at the lens.
feasibility fix: Write one continuous 10 s action without per-shot durations or a 1.5 s hook, e.g. 'her open hand rises slowly and a thin path of starlight gradually appears below it'.
feasibility fix: Drop the exact return to frame 1 and end on the held gesture, or a simple slow fade.

concept.title: Two Stars
concept.logline: Tara's third eye slowly glows, and the guiding star above her crown brightens in answer, washing her face and jewelry in cool light.
concept.hook: Within the first second a soft glow begins to gather at her third eye, and the star above her crown starts to grow brighter.
concept.story: Tara is the Saving Star: the light a lost traveler steers by. Her third eye and the star above her crown are two lights answering each other. It shows that her guidance is both her own sight and the light she hangs in the sky for others.
concept.loop: Both lights ease back to their faint first-frame glow, and the cool light on her crown and silver fades away. The final frame matches the opening frame exactly, so the glow can begin again.
concept.share_trigger: Sent as a quiet, comforting good-night message, or to someone who needs to feel looked after. Easy to send with a line like 'someone is watching over you.'
concept.caption_hook: She is the star you steer by, and she is watching over you tonight.
concept.audio: A soft, high shimmering tone that slowly rises, with distant wind-chime notes. A deep, warm hum underneath gives it body.

shots.camera: Straight-on at eye level, locked off, waist-up, crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: Her eyes stay calm and level on the viewer while a soft sapphire glow slowly gathers in her third eye, making the skin around it shine. Her black hair settles gradually under its own weight.
shots.purpose: A visible change begins right away on the most recognisable part of her face, so the viewer's eyes go to it at once.

shots.camera: Same straight-on eye-level framing, locked off, crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: The guiding star above her crown brightens to match her third eye, and a cool blue-white light spreads down over her crown, face, skull garland and silver jewelry so they gleam. Then both lights slowly settle back to their faint opening glow.
shots.purpose: The payoff is the star answering her eye. It joins her to the sky and shows the star is her light. The settling back closes the loop.

feedback: virality: The hook is a faint glow gathering at the third eye. It is subtle on a phone, and a viewer scrolling at speed will read it as a still portrait, so it fails the 1.5-second 'visible, specific motion' test.

virality: It is essentially the 'goddess stands there' scene the rubric penalises: a locked, straight-on portrait where the only change is lighting. There is no action and no consequence in the world, only brightness changing.

virality: The 'guiding star above her crown' is not in the dossier or the locked anchor description. It is an unsupported element that may not render, and the 'two lights answering' idea is abstract and needs a caption to explain.
virality: The payoff is a light wash over jewelry. It is pretty but not a moment a viewer grasps instantly, and it is not tied to her story of crossing, saving or protecting.
virality: Loop is mechanically clean because the final frame matches the first, but nothing happens in between to make a viewer want to watch again.

virality: Send-worthiness is a soft 'good-night, someone is watching over you', which is pleasant but generic. Save value is low, and novelty versus generic AI devotional glow clips is low, since glowing eyes on a goddess portrait is the standard output.

authenticity: Best match to the 'star' reading of her name and the third eye, and non-graphic. But the claim 'her third eye and the star above her crown are two lights answering each other' is invented iconography. The dossier mentions no star above her crown, and 'a guiding star above her crown' is not documented in her imagery. The third eye is a general Shaiva/Shakta feature, not a specific 'sight she shares with the sky' symbol.
authenticity: Presents 'Saving Star' as established. The star reading is one of three disputed etymologies, and the sailors'-guide line comes from the dossier as only one reading.

authenticity: The caption 'she is watching over you tonight' and the 'good-night message' framing is cozy and comforting. It misses her wrathful, protective, tantric character and reads closer to a lullaby than to a Mahavidya. A devotee might find it soft but not offensive.

authenticity: 'Sapphire glow' and 'cool blue-white light' on the skull garland is fine and non-graphic, but the garland is mentioned only as something that gleams. The dossier says the skulls stand for the letters of the alphabet. Highlighting them without context risks an exoticised or macabre read.
authenticity: Hair mismatch persists ('black hair settles'), contradicting the matted jata/Ekajata iconography.

feasibility: The concept depends on a 'guiding star above her crown' and a 'faint first-frame glow' on both the third eye and the star. The dossier does not list a star in the anchor. If the reference portrait lacks it, the clip fails the rule against content that is in frame 1 but not in the reference.

feasibility: The cool light spreading over her crown, face, skull garland and jewelry is a global relighting effect. Video models often flicker or shift skin tone and detail when asked for this, and it could turn the skin from blue to white.
feasibility: It says 'silver jewelry', but the dossier describes gold, pearls and bone ornaments. Check this against the anchor so the model is not told to change the metal.
feasibility: 'Final frame matches the opening frame exactly' is unrealistic. Small drift is likely, and the loop should not rely on an exact match.
feasibility: The 5 s plus 5 s shot split and the 'within the first second' hook rely on timing. It should read as one continuous clip.
virality fix: Give the light a consequence in the world. For example, her third-eye flash lights a single star in the sky, and that star drops a beam that lights a whole path or dark water below.
virality fix: Make the first 1.5 seconds a sharp event: the third eye snaps open from closed, with a visible pulse of light. Opening an eye is unambiguous motion even on a small screen.
virality fix: Replace the unsourced crown star with a dossier-grounded device, such as the sea or the starlight path, or drop it. Keep one image only.
virality fix: Tie it to the story: the eye-light is what the lost sailor steers by, so show a point of light travelling out from her eye across dark water.
virality fix: If the glow idea is kept, make the change large and fast (dark to bright), not a slow swell.

authenticity fix: Either remove the 'star above her crown' as a fixed iconographic element or label it as a symbolic, artistic device in the story ('a star appears as the light she is named for'). Do not claim it as traditional iconography.
authenticity fix: Qualify the name: 'Tara means star, and also saviour', so the star meaning is not the only reading.
authenticity fix: Add a note of protection and strength to the caption (guide and protector), so she does not read as only a gentle night-light.
authenticity fix: If the garland is lit, keep the framing tasteful and, if possible, reference the 'letters of the alphabet' meaning in the caption.
authenticity fix: Fix or avoid the loose-hair motion.

feasibility fix: Confirm that the star above the crown and a dim third-eye glow are visible in the reference portrait. If not, remove the star and make it a single-element piece: third eye glow plus a soft light bloom on the face.
feasibility fix: Limit the light spread to the face and crown, and name the garland and jewelry only as 'catching a little light'. Say that the skin stays blue.
feasibility fix: Write the action as one continuous sequence, 'the third eye slowly glows, the star brightens in answer, then both ease back', with no second-based beats.
feasibility fix: Describe the loop as 'ease back toward the opening glow', not an exact match.

concept.title: The Water Goes Still
concept.logline: Tara slowly lowers her open palm, and a restless dark sea beneath her settles into a still mirror full of stars.
concept.hook: In the first 1.5 seconds her palm starts to lower, and dark, restless water swells into view at the bottom of the frame.
concept.story: Tara is the protector who steps in when danger comes suddenly, and the one who calms the poisoned sea in her story. The clip shows that calm in one simple movement: a lowered hand, and trouble becomes still water.
concept.loop: Her palm rises slowly out of the lower frame, the mirror-still water sinks away below the frame edge, and the sky behind her is as it was at the start, ready for the palm to lower again.
concept.share_trigger: Sent to an anxious or overwhelmed friend with 'breathe, it will settle.' Also saved for calming moments, and for people interested in protective goddess imagery.
concept.caption_hook: Whatever is churning inside you, let it settle like this.
concept.audio: Low, rolling water sounds that soften into silence as the sea calms. A slow, deep breath-like pad plays underneath, and one soft chime sounds at the moment of stillness.

shots.camera: Straight-on at eye level, locked off, waist-up, crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: Her open palm turns downward and begins to lower slowly. As it moves, a dark sea with faint, restless currents swells into the lower edge of the frame. Her black hair settles gradually under its own weight.
shots.purpose: Motion starts at once and shows the problem: troubled water. Her palm is the response the viewer is waiting for.

shots.camera: Same straight-on eye-level framing, locked off, crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: Her palm hovers low and steady, and the currents in the water fade until the surface becomes a still black mirror that reflects the stars and her cool glow. Then her palm rises slowly and the water sinks out of view below the frame.
shots.purpose: The payoff is the instant of stillness: she calms the water with one movement. The palm rising and the water leaving return the frame to the opening portrait.

feedback: virality: Strongest concept: it has a clear cause and effect (palm lowers, the sea goes from churning to a still mirror) and one instantly graspable transformation. It also matches the dossier's calming-the-poisoned-sea beat and the 'sudden danger' protection theme.

virality: The hook promises motion, but the water that 'swells into view at the bottom' with 'faint, restless currents' is low contrast. If the churn is faint, the before and after will not differ enough on a phone screen, and the payoff is weakened. The turbulence needs to be dramatic first.
virality: The calming arrives at about second 5 to 6, after a slow lowering palm. The tension is not built hard enough early, so a scroller may leave before the water settles.

virality: Loop is weak: the palm rises and the water sinks away, which is a reversal rather than a return to a recognisable first frame. The last 2 seconds are an exit, so the viewer sees an ending and not a restart.

virality: A downward-pushing palm on a locked waist-up shot means the water sits at the very bottom edge and may be mostly cropped. The still-mirror reflection of stars needs enough frame area to be seen.

virality: Send-worthiness is strong ('breathe, it will settle' to an anxious friend). The calming effect also has save value as a relaxation clip. Novelty is moderate: the 'calming hand' is relatively common, but the churn-to-mirror contrast is a clean visual.

authenticity: Closest tie to the dossier's main narrative: the churning of the ocean and the poison, and her calming role. But the dossier flags the poison story as devotional tradition, not in the main Puranic accounts, with variant identities of the goddess (Tara, Durga, Parvati). The story line 'the one who calms the poisoned sea in her story' presents it as settled. The 'poisoned sea' framing is also a loose conflation: in the legend the poison burns Shiva and Tara cools it with her milk. She does not still the sea.

authenticity: Caption and share text ('breathe, it will settle', 'whatever is churning inside you') read as a wellness/anxiety trope, which flattens her protective power into a calming meditation clip. It also lacks any mention of the poison, Shiva or Tarapith, so the connection is only an inference.

authenticity: A downward-lowered palm over water is not a documented gesture of hers. It resembles a generic 'peace be still' motif (a Christian gospel echo), which risks mixing traditions without care.
authenticity: Hair mismatch persists; the anchor's identifying features are never shown in the action.

feasibility: The action begins with 'her open palm turns downward and begins to lower', which assumes a raised open palm is already in frame 1. The dossier says the anchor omits hand objects and gestures, so this is probably not in the reference portrait. If it is not, the first frame has to invent the hand.

feasibility: Too many moving elements: the palm lowering, a restless sea swelling in, currents fading, the surface turning into a mirror, reflections of stars and her glow, then the palm rising and the water sinking away. That is far beyond two.

feasibility: The mirror reflecting the stars and her glow requires physically coherent reflections of a scene that is not fully visible. Reflections are a common failure and are likely to shimmer or look wrong.

feasibility: Water 'swells into the lower edge' of a locked-off waist-up frame, with no ground plane or source, and then 'sinks out of view'. This is implausible motion with weak cause and effect, since a lowered palm calming churning water has no physical link.
feasibility: The restless-to-still transition (fading currents) is subtle and hard to render. It could just read as static water from the start.
feasibility: Rising palm, sinking water and an exact return to the opening frame add a long reverse sequence. The 4 s and 6 s split plus the '1.5 second' hook are timing-dependent.
virality fix: Open with violent, high-contrast churning: whitecaps or dark waves slamming up the lower third in frame 1, so the problem is obvious in the first second.

virality fix: Let the palm lowering do the work immediately. Have the waves visibly flatten in sync with the palm descent over about 3 seconds, then hold the mirror and starry reflection for 3 to 4 seconds as the payoff.
virality fix: Give the water about the bottom 40 percent of the frame so the mirror and its star reflections are readable on a phone.

virality fix: Make the loop clean: end with the palm and sea returning to the churn at the same pose and position as the first frame, or start on the still mirror and have the churn arrive, so the last frame matches the first.
virality fix: Time the chime exactly to the moment the last ripple dies so the stillness lands as a beat.

concept.title: She Calms the Water
concept.logline: Tara lowers her open hand over dark churning water, the sea calms, and a path of starlight opens toward the viewer.
concept.hook: In the first second, dark swells heave up into the lower frame while her open hand starts to lower toward them, so the screen is moving from the very start.
concept.story: Her name is read as star, as saviour, and as the one who ferries you across the ocean of worldly life. Devotional tradition also tells of her calming the poison of the churning ocean. Here she is a protector with real strength: her hand stills rough water, and the path of starlight that forms is the way across. It is a symbolic scene drawn from these readings, not a fixed image from her traditional iconography.
concept.loop: The calm water and its starlight path sink gently below the lower edge of the frame, and her hand returns to rest. The sky and portrait ease back toward the opening, so the heaving swells can rise again as the clip restarts.
concept.share_trigger: Sent to a friend or family member going through a rough stretch, with a line like 'the water will settle, and there is a way across.' It works as a reassurance people will save for hard days.
concept.caption_hook: Tara means star, saviour, and the one who carries you across. When the water is at its wildest, she is the one who calms it.
concept.audio: A low, rolling swell of dark water and a deep drone at the start. As the sea calms, the water hushes and soft, clear chime notes appear one by one, with a warm low hum underneath.

shots.purpose: Large, readable motion from the first second: rough dark water rises and her hand answers it. The gesture and the water reacting to it are easy to follow on a small screen.

shots.camera: Same straight-on eye-level framing, locked off, crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: The water spreads out smooth and still beneath her hand, and a path of starlight forms on its surface, stretching toward the viewer. Then her hand rests, and the water and path sink slowly below the lower edge of the frame, leaving the starry sky and her portrait close to how the clip began.
shots.purpose: The payoff is that she calms the water and shows the way across, which ties directly to her saving and ferrying role. The sinking water makes the loop seamless without needing an exact frame match.

feedback: virality: The hook is much stronger. Heaving dark swells in the lower frame with her hand lowering is large, readable motion from frame 1, and the cause-and-effect (hand lowers, water flattens) is a clear, instant consequence.

virality: The risk is rendering. Water flattening under a hand, hair settling 'under its own weight' and a starlight path forming on a surface are several simultaneous physical effects. Video models often make the water calm unconvincingly or ignore the hand, and the settling hair is a needless extra beat.

virality: The loop is weaker than claimed. Everything sinking out of frame and the hand returning to rest is a quiet reset, and it relies on the model returning near the original portrait. The re-rising swells at the restart are a plausible but not guaranteed flow.

virality: The hand lowers 'over the water' and 'palm down' with no clear sense of whether the water is in front of or below her, which may cause spatial confusion in a waist-up frame.

The story says 'devotional tradition also tells' and 'symbolic scene,' which is good, but the caption ('she is the one who calms it') states it as plain fact with no qualifier.

Turning it into 'her hand stills the sea' departs from the tale and generalises it; a devotee may find it a loose, even sanitised, reading, though it is respectful.

concept.title: The Calming of the Dark Water
concept.logline: Tara raises her open hand over churning dark water, which calms into a path of starlight leading across to the viewer.
concept.hook: From the first second, heavy dark water swells up from the bottom edge of the portrait and churns across the lower frame, while Tara's steady, stern gaze holds the viewer and her hand rises.
concept.story: Tara is read as the star that guides, the saviour, and the one who carries across the ocean of worldly existence. Her devotional story tells of the poisoned sea that she calms. This clip is a symbolic rendering of the 'carries across' reading, not a fixed traditional scene. Dark water churns below her, and her raised open hand settles it. The still surface then carries a path of starlight that runs out toward the viewer, so the crossing is shown, not just told. Her stern, protective gaze keeps her a rescuer, not a gentle ornament. Blue skin, third eye, tiger-skin wrap, skull garland and serpent ornaments stay clear. Her loose hair follows the portrait and departs from the matted or single-braid forms in the tradition.

Her open hand lowers, and a road of stars lights up under it as the way across. It is a symbolic scene drawn from these readings, not a fixed image from her traditional iconography. One devotional tradition also tells of her calming the poison of the churning ocean, and the versions of that story differ. Her tiger-skin wrap, skull garland and serpent ornaments stay visible, so she reads as the strong guardian, not a generic gentle figure.
concept.loop: The clip ends on the held image of the glowing star path and her lowered hand. The path is made of the same stars as the sky, so the last frame sits close to the opening sky. A soft dissolve then lets the path fade back into the sky as the clip restarts.
concept.share_trigger: Sent to a friend or family member in a hard stretch, with a line like 'there is a way across, and you are not alone.' It works as a reassurance people save for difficult days.
concept.caption_hook: Tara's name is read as star, saviour, and the one who carries you across. Here she lights the way, a symbolic scene drawn from those readings.
concept.audio: A low, deep drone and a soft held breath of wind at the start. As the first star flares, clear chime notes sound one by one, rising in pace as the path fills with stars. A warm low hum sits underneath until the end.

concept.title: The Stilling of the Dark Water
concept.logline: Tara presses her open hand down, and a dark swell below her flattens into glassy water carrying one bright line of stars.
concept.hook: The calm starry portrait holds for a heartbeat, then one heavy dark swell heaves up along the bottom edge as her open hand lowers toward it with a stern, level gaze.
concept.story: Tara's name is read as the star that guides, the saviour, and the one who ferries across the ocean of worldly existence. This clip is a symbolic picture of that crossing, not a fixed traditional scene. Rough dark water rises below her, her hand presses down toward it, and it goes glassy with one bright line of stars laid across it like a path. Her gaze is direct and stern, so she reads as a rescuer and not a gentle ornament. A devotional tradition, not found in the main Puranic accounts and told in different versions, says she saved Shiva from the poison of the churned ocean. The clip only echoes that tale. Blue skin, third eye, tiger-skin wrap, skull garland and serpent ornaments stay clear. Her loose hair is a stylisation; traditional images show matted locks or a single braid.
concept.loop: The last frame is a held image of still black water holding a line of stars beneath her, mirroring the starry sky of the first frame. The restart to the bare portrait reads as the water becoming sky again, so the rough water can rise anew.
concept.share_trigger: Devotees of Tara and people curious about the ten great wisdom goddesses send it as a clear image of her as rescuer and ferrier across. Viewers who love satisfying moments of rough water going still share it too.
concept.caption_hook: Tara, second of the ten great wisdom goddesses, is the star that guides and the one who ferries across. Her loose hair here is a stylisation; traditional images show matted locks or a single braid.
concept.audio: A deep, heavy water rumble that drops to a hush the moment her hand stops. A soft low drone follows, with one clear, gentle tone as the line of stars appears.

shots.camera: Straight-on at eye level, locked off, waist-up, crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: A single heavy swell of dark water rises low along the bottom edge, below her waist and clear of her garland and wrap, while her right hand lowers into view with the palm open and facing down, and the swell flattens where her palm stops above it.
shots.purpose: Cause and effect read at once: dark water rises, her hand presses down, and the swell collapses. Her stern three-eyed gaze marks her as a rescuer.

shots.camera: Same locked straight-on eye-level framing, crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: Her palm stays steady above the water, and the last ripples spread outward and fade until the surface is glassy black, and a single bright line of pale stars forms across it, its soft glow touching her skull garland. Her hair settles gently under its own weight, and the final image holds.
shots.purpose: The payoff arrives and stays: rough water becomes still, with a clear line of stars as the path across. The held final image is the shareable picture of Tara as protector.

feedback: virality: Hook is weak. The first beat is a 'calm starry portrait [that] holds for a heartbeat', which is a static goddess-stands-there opening. The swell only arrives after that, so visible motion misses the 1.5s window.

virality: The swell is confined to the bottom edge, below her waist, and her hand has to 'lower into view'. On a phone the action sits in a thin strip at the bottom and may be hidden by UI overlays and captions. The cause and effect is small and easy to miss.

virality: Shot 1 asks for three things in 3 seconds: a swell rising, a hand entering, and the swell flattening. The video model may blur these into mush, and the cause and effect may not read cleanly.

virality: Shot 2 is 7 seconds of mostly stillness: a steady palm, fading ripples, a faint star line. That is a slow back half with no new development. Retention will sag, and people may swipe away before the payoff.

virality: Loop logic is muddy. The end is a still black water with a star line, but the start is a calm starry portrait with no water. The 'water becoming sky again' idea is conceptual, and a viewer will see a jump cut, not a seamless loop.

virality: The hand pressing down is a gentle gesture that the story calls 'stern'. The hand is read as hushing or patting the water, not rescuing. It lacks the stakes of danger, and nothing is actually saved or crossed.
virality: Send-worthiness is thin and niche: devotees plus 'satisfying calm water' viewers. There is no clear person to send it to, and no emotional line to attach.
virality: Save value is low. It is a pretty image, with no knowledge, caption payload or reason to keep it.
virality: Novelty is only moderate. Calming water with a starry glow is a familiar AI devotional trope, though the downward press is a slightly fresher gesture than the usual raised palm.

authenticity: Strong match to the dossier's recommended beat 1 (calming the poisoned sea), and the 'crossing over' meaning is expressed. It flags the scene as symbolic, not canonical, and the poison tale as devotional, not Puranic, with versions differing. That is honest handling.

authenticity: The hand presses DOWN onto the water. In Indian iconography a raised open palm is the protective gesture (abhaya). A downward-facing palm reads as dominating or suppressing the sea, not rescuing. A devotee may find it more 'commanding' than 'guiding', and it drifts from the 'ferrier / guide' meaning toward control.

authenticity: The water is meant as the 'ocean of samsara' and also echoes the poison. The story text blends the two without saying which. The 'dark swell' could read as the poison, but nothing in the visuals distinguishes it.

authenticity: 'Hair settles gently under its own weight' draws extra attention to the loose hair, which departs from the matted or single-braid iconography. The caption and story disclose it, but the beat itself spotlights the departure.

authenticity: The line of stars 'touching her skull garland' is an invented flourish. It is harmless but mixes the garland, which stands for the alphabet, with the star path. Keep the garland incidental.

authenticity: Scale: the scene is waist-up with the water 'below her waist', so there is no standing-on-Shiva or cremation-ground context. That is fine and avoids sensitive imagery, but the 'star' and 'ferry' readings rely heavily on the caption, since the on-screen scene shows a hand and still water, not a crossing.
authenticity: The stern gaze is used to read as a 'rescuer'. Sternness is acceptable for Ugra Tara but should not tip into anger directed at the viewer.

feasibility: Frame 1 is the plain starry portrait, which is correct. But her right hand "lowers into view", so it enters the frame from outside. The reference is waist-up and the hand may not be visible there. Hands that enter mid-clip tend to render with distorted fingers.

feasibility: There are three distinct moving elements besides settling hair: the swell rising and flattening, the descending hand, and the star line forming with its glow. That is over the limit of two.

feasibility: The cause and effect is symbolic. The palm hovers above the water and never touches it, so the swell flattening reads as magic rather than visible physics. The model may flatten the water before the hand arrives, or ignore the hand.

feasibility: The water must appear from nothing along the bottom edge of a portrait that has none, and it must be kept clear of the garland and wrap. This is an unreferenced new element that could creep up over her body or garland.
feasibility: The star line's glow "touching her skull garland" adds a light-interaction effect on a detailed ornament. It is the sort of fine detail that tends to flicker or morph.

feasibility: The brief depends on timing: a 3 s swell-and-collapse, then 7 s of ripples fading, the star line forming and the hair settling. Seedance will not hit that split reliably. The swell could take the whole clip, or the ripples could be skipped.

feasibility: Hair is described as settling under its own weight, but the shot also asks for a static, locked-off hold. A clear action sequence in a 10 s clip with a mostly idle second half risks drifting or a wandering camera.
virality fix: Cut the calm portrait opener. Open on frame 1 with the swell already heaving high and the hand already moving, so motion starts at 0.0s.
virality fix: Raise the water to chest or shoulder height and put it in the middle of the frame, so the threat and the press are the dominant visual and survive the phone UI crop.

virality fix: Shorten to a tighter structure: about 2s of violent swell, a 1s press and collapse, then a short payoff. Let the star line draw itself toward the viewer so there is a travelling motion in the back half.

virality fix: Fill the back half with one new, simple beat, such as the star path unrolling toward the camera as the crossing. This delivers the 'ferries across' meaning and gives a reason to stay to the end.

virality fix: Fix the loop by making the first frame match the last. Start on the starlit still water and have the swell rise from it, or end with the water darkening back into the opening state, so the restart is seamless.
virality fix: Make the press forceful and decisive, with a visible consequence such as a shockwave ring flattening the swell outward, so she reads as a rescuer and not a hush.
virality fix: Add a text-free hook in the caption that gives a send target ('send this to someone crossing a rough night') and one line of meaning for saves.

authenticity fix: Change the gesture to a level, open-palm hold (hovering or extended toward the water) instead of pressing down, or have the palm face outward in abhaya as the water settles, so protection, not domination, is the read.
authenticity fix: Make the star path run toward the viewer, as in the dossier's beat 1, so it reads as a way across rather than a line lying on the water.
authenticity fix: Drop the hair-settling detail and the star glow touching the garland. Keep the disclosure in the caption only.
authenticity fix: Soften the gaze from 'stern' to 'steady, watchful, compassionate-fierce' so the devotee reads a mother who protects, in line with Bamakhepa's 'my children' devotion.
authenticity fix: In the caption, name the 'ocean of existence' meaning plainly and state that the poison echo is from a devotional tradition.

feasibility fix: Drop the hand entering frame. Start with the hand already visible in the reference, or use a small downward palm motion that is already in frame. If neither works, remove the hand and let her gaze and the water carry the cause.
feasibility fix: Cut to two moving elements. Keep the swell calming into glassy water and let the star line appear as part of the water's change, with no separate glow on the garland.
feasibility fix: Remove the second-by-second structure. Describe one continuous sequence, "the dark swell slowly settles into glassy water as the stars appear", without a 3 s/7 s split.
feasibility fix: Let the water be a low band at the very bottom of the frame, well below the waist, and say nothing about reaching her ornaments.

concept.title: She Stills the Dark Sea
concept.logline: Tara raises one steady hand and the dark, churning sea behind her goes still, mirroring the stars.
concept.hook: In the first second a dark sea rises into view behind her, its swells rolling restlessly, as her stern gaze holds and her hand begins to lift against the danger.
concept.story: Tara's name is read as star, as saviour, and as the one who ferries you across the ocean of worldly life. She is the second of the ten great wisdom goddesses, a protector who steps in when danger comes suddenly. A rough dark sea is the danger. Her raised open palm is a guarding gesture, and the sea stills into a mirror of her stars, so the crossing becomes visible as a calm, star-lit water. Her three eyes stay stern and watchful, and her blue skin, tiger-skin wrap, skull garland and serpent ornaments stay in view, so she reads as a fierce guardian. This is a symbolic scene, not a fixed temple image. Her hair is shown loose, while tradition more often shows it matted or in a single braid. One devotional telling also says she calmed the poison of the churning sea, and versions of that tale differ.
concept.loop: The final frame is her centered portrait with the same star-filled sky, now doubled in the still water, so the ending looks like the opening sky made whole. When the clip restarts, the sky returns to its first stillness and the dark sea rises again, so the calm at the end feeds straight back into the threat at the start.
concept.share_trigger: Sent to someone in a frightening or stormy stretch, such as a hard diagnosis, a night journey or a crisis at home, with a line like 'may she still this for you.' It is a protector image, saved and sent by people who know her as the one who guards you from sudden danger.
concept.caption_hook: Tara, second of the ten great wisdom goddesses, is the star, the saviour and the one who ferries you across. Here her raised hand stills a dark sea. A symbolic scene, with her hair loose where tradition shows it matted or braided.
concept.audio: A low, deep rumble of restless water and a held, tense drone at the start. As her hand reaches full height, the rumble drops away to a hush, and one deep, clear bell tone sounds and rings out over a soft, steady hum until the end.

shots.camera: Straight-on at eye level, locked off, waist-up, crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: A dark sea rises into view behind her, its horizon at chest height and its swells rolling restlessly on both sides of her body. Her three eyes hold the viewer in a stern, steady gaze as her right hand lifts slowly to chest height with the palm open and facing forward, and as it rises the swells begin to slow and flatten.
shots.purpose: The problem is on screen from the first second: a dark rough sea. One large, slow gesture is the cause, and the calming water is the visible effect, easy to read on a small screen.

shots.camera: Same straight-on eye-level framing, locked off, crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: Her hand holds steady at chest height, palm forward, and the sea goes fully still, so the stars of the night sky appear in the water and a bright band of reflected starlight spreads across the calm surface on both sides of her. Her stern gaze stays on the viewer as the clip ends on this held image.
shots.purpose: The payoff is a before and after: restless dark water becomes a still, star-filled mirror. It shows protection from danger and a safe crossing in one clear change, and the final frame echoes the opening sky.

feedback: virality: The hook is better than A's. The dark sea is on screen in the first second with rolling swells. But the sea 'rises into view', which implies a fade-in, and her hand lifts 'slowly'. The first 1.5s is atmospheric motion in the background, not one decisive action.

virality: The slow 5-second hand lift is a classic raised-palm pose, the most generic devotional gesture. Her stillness and the slow pace mean the calming effect reads as gradual and soft, not a strong cause-and-effect beat.

virality: Shot 2 is a hold. The sea is already still and the hand does not move, with only a starlight band spreading. About 5 seconds of near stillness at the end risks a drop-off, and the payoff reveal is modest.

virality: The sea in the background with swells on both sides of her body, plus the star reflection, asks the model to render a lot of coherent water and a mirror reflection. Reflections of a night sky in still water are a common failure point, and the background may flicker.

virality: The loop claim is partly weak. The ending has the stars 'doubled in the still water' while the opening is the 'same star-filled sky' with a dark rough sea. It matches the sky, but the water state differs, so the restart is a hard cut from calm to storm. It is arguably a fine hard-cut loop, but it is not seamless.
virality: Her raised palm facing forward reads more as 'stop' or blessing than as rescue or ferrying. Nothing is carried or crossed, so the 'ferrier' meaning is only in the caption.
virality: The save value is modest. It is a pretty protector image, though the share framing is stronger than A's.

authenticity: Closely aligned with the dossier: the sea as 'ocean of existence', protection from sudden danger, and a raised open palm that reads as a classic protective (abhaya-like) gesture. This is the more iconographically natural gesture of the two concepts.
authenticity: It discloses that the scene is symbolic, that the hair is loose where tradition shows matted or braided, and that the poison story is devotional and varies. Good caution handling.

authenticity: The sea is placed behind her at chest height with swells on both sides. A restless sea at chest height could crowd her torso and ornaments, and 'against the danger' makes her a fighter of the sea, not a guide across. The 'ferrier' meaning is shown only as calm water, with no path or crossing.
authenticity: The hook says her hand lifts 'against the danger', which frames her as combative toward the sea. The dossier's meaning is rescue and crossing, so the framing leans slightly off.

authenticity: The share trigger suggests sending it to people with 'a hard diagnosis' with 'may she still this for you'. It is sincere, but it turns a deity image into a personal-crisis message template. A devotee might accept this, but it risks sentimentality, so the caption should not push it.

authenticity: The loop claims the sky is 'doubled' in the water and the 'sea rises again' at restart. Fine, but the star mirror gives no explicit guide or path, so the 'star' etymology is only implied.
authenticity: The audio says 'one deep, clear bell tone'. A bell is a generic temple cue and acceptable, but it should not suggest a specific ritual practice.

feasibility: Frame 1 already contains a dark rough sea behind her with its horizon at chest height. The reference portrait has a starry sky, so this is a new element in frame 1 that is absent from the reference. That is a direct rubric failure. The hook text ("rises into view") also contradicts the shot description (sea already at chest height).

feasibility: The whole background has to be swapped from sky to sea around her silhouette, with swells "on both sides of her body". Rendering that without bleeding into her hair, shoulders and garland is a heavy compositing job.
feasibility: There are four or more moving elements: rolling swells, the lifting hand, swells slowing, and the star reflections and a spreading band of light. That is well beyond two.
feasibility: A palm raised forward toward the camera involves foreshortening and a hand moving to chest height across her ornaments and garland. This is a likely source of finger and anatomy errors.

feasibility: The stars "appear in the water" and a reflected band "spreads" on both sides. A reflection that mirrors the sky while the figure and sky are static is physically tricky, and the model may produce a plain glow instead.

feasibility: The brief depends on timing, with a 5 s and 5 s split: the swells slow as the hand rises, then the sea goes fully still once the hand holds. The loop claim of the sky "doubled in the still water" also needs a sky and a horizon layout that is not in the reference.
feasibility: The hand's cause and effect is plausible as a gesture of authority, but the sea responds to a raised hand at a distance with no physical link, so the cause reads as vague.
virality fix: Start with the sea already churning hard and the hand already mid-rise at 0.0s, with no fade-in, so the first frame carries the threat and the motion.

virality fix: Speed up the gesture. Make the palm snap up decisively around 1.5 to 2s, and have the sea flatten in a clear outward wave from her hand, so the cause and effect is unmistakable and not a slow fade.

virality fix: Shorten the settle and use the back half for one new beat, such as a path of starlight running from her feet toward the camera, which says 'crossing' and gives a visual reward in place of a hold.
virality fix: Simplify the background. Keep the horizon low and the reflection to one bright band of stars, to avoid flicker from a full mirrored sky.
virality fix: Make the loop tighter by having the end image begin to darken or ripple in the final 0.5s, so the cut back to the rough sea feels continuous.
virality fix: Keep and sharpen the share angle. The line 'may she still this for you' is the strongest send hook across both concepts, so put it on the caption's first line.
authenticity fix: Reword the hook and shot 1 so her hand lifts 'in protection' and not 'against the danger'. The sea settles in her presence, not as a battle.
authenticity fix: Lower the horizon or sea so it stays clear of her chest, garland and serpent ornaments, and keep the iconography fully readable.
authenticity fix: Add a subtle path of starlight leading from her toward the viewer on the still water to carry the 'guide / ferrier across' meaning, as in the dossier's beat 1.
authenticity fix: Keep the caption's disclosures, and leave out any prompt to send the clip with a specific blessing or in medical crisis. Let viewers decide how to share it.
authenticity fix: Keep the poison reference in the caption as 'a devotional telling' and avoid implying the clip depicts that story.
feasibility fix: Begin on the exact reference portrait with the starry sky and no sea. Let the dark water rise in from the bottom edge during the clip rather than being present from frame 1.
feasibility fix: Cut to two moving elements: the water calming and one slow hand gesture. Drop the spreading reflection band and just have the stars show on the calm surface.
feasibility fix: Use a hand pose that is already in the reference, or a very small lift of an open palm, instead of a large raise to chest height facing the camera.
feasibility fix: Do not put water on both sides of her body. Keep it as a low band at the bottom, away from the silhouette.
